messages.subject: multilevel bym model question
parts:
I would like to run a 2 level model in which one level is individuals, and a second level is areal units into which the individuals aggregate (zip codes).

I've started off with the following:

model1 <- inla( result ~ race + mage + gender+ sdi +
                f(zipcode, model = "iid") +
                f(zipcode, model="bym", graph=w_zips) ,
                data = data ,
                family = "binomial",
                control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE) )

I'm adding the iid term for zipcode because the fixed variable sdi is a feature of the zipcodes and not the individuals.

A couple questions -
 Does this syntax look ok?
 The neighborhood matrix w_zips is one I've made with sf using nb2mat - can that be used for the bym models in INLA?

The dataset is 96,000 individuals aggregated into 700 zip codes.

Thanks for any advice.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] multilevel bym model question
parts:
Hi,

it would be easier it you wrote the model in math as well.

there are a couple of issues though

- you have two names that is the same 'zipcode' for the iid model and
'zipcode' for the bym. I should give an error running it, but the
solution is simepl

data$zipcode2 = data$zipcode

and use zipcode2 in one of the two places

- the iid with zipcode adds another iid effect to the already exissting
one in 'bym' (see inla.doc("bym")), unless you want to use
model="besag" instead of 'bym'.

- yes, I think nb2mat can me used to define the matrix,but if its
'weighted' beyond the 0-1 weight, that would not be used, as the
'besag' model is predefined for 0-1 weights.

- you can check this with the example in nb2mat

> g = inla.read.graph(col005.w.mat)

which will give an inla-graph object.
